headline: Volumes soften, but WillScot lifts its full-year outlook
summary_short: WillScot's Q1 2026 revenue fell 2.0% y/y to $548.6 million and net income dropped 34.7% to $28.1 million on restructuring charges, even as Adjusted EBITDA of $211.0 million (-7.8% y/y) topped plan and management raised its full-year 2026 outlook.
summary_long: Revenue fell 2.0% y/y to $548.6M as a 7.3% drop in average units on rent and a $13.4M decline in new-unit sales outweighed 12.3% higher delivery/installation revenue from large complex projects. Gross margin fell to 52.1% from 53.7% on higher leasing costs and receivables write-offs. SG&A fell 1.8% to $154.0M. Adjusted EBITDA was $211.0M (-7.8% y/y, ~38.5% margin). Net income fell 34.7% to $28.1M, mostly on $11.6M of Network Optimization Plan restructuring charges. Rental-equipment capex rose to $101.9M funding large-project activations; Net CAPEX was $89.3M. WillScot paid a $0.07/share dividend, repurchased $7.3M of stock, and raised its full-year 2026 outlook to roughly $2.25B revenue (from ~$2.18B) and $915M Adjusted EBITDA.
